turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mr Iyer, while you were parking, your wife at the counter told me the burning in both feet is there every night, since last winter she thinks. And the pharmacy label on the file says Lantus, insulin glargine, 24 units at bedtime.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Twenty-four units? No, I dial eighteen. My wife, she always answers for me, but she has made that foot business sound worse than—
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please come through, Mr Iyer. I am Dr Mehta. The counter note is in front of me. You are fifty-eight, with type 2 diabetes, on tablets and insulin, is that right?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, fifty-eight in March. The diabetes, I cannot date it properly, around five-ish years or maybe six, after my father fell ill. Tablets from the start, and the insulin they added later, I forget which year.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): We will sort the dates as far as we can. What made you come in today?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The sugar, mainly. At home the fasting was one-eighty-something, or was it one-nine-zero, the strip looked faint and the morning light in the kitchen is poor. And the feet, after standing in the shop. The scooter parking outside your clinic is also very tight, that is a separate headache.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): One moment, the parking we will leave. Kavitha, the checks you did outside?

[SEG0008] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Capillary glucose two hundred and fourteen. Blood pressure one forty-eight over eighty-six, pulse eighty-two, oxygen saturation ninety-eight percent. He had tea in the waiting area, so this is not a fasting sample.

[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): So today we have glucose 214, not fasting, BP 148/86, pulse 82, saturation 98. I will not use that home one-eighty-something as a real number. Tell me the tablets as you actually swallow them.

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Metformin, the large tablet, 1000 mg, morning and night, after food. Glimepiride 2 mg, only in the morning, before breakfast, and that one I do not skip. The insulin is the confusing part, if I may explain properly.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please do. You started to say eighteen units.

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Lantus, the glargine, at night. I dial eighteen. Your label says twenty-four, and some nights if the sugar felt high I have dialled twenty, so even I am not clean about it. Maybe the other clinic reduced it, or maybe I reduced it, I cannot remember which.
[SEG0013] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Doctor, the last bottle we dispensed is still labelled 24 units at bedtime. There is no later letter scanned in the file, I did look twice.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then we simply have two doses and no way to know the current one. I am not changing any insulin figure today. Do you inject it every night, or not really?

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Weekends, yes, after dinner. On work days I shut the shop late, nine or ten, and sometimes I have only had biscuits, so I skip the injection, three or four nights a week, maybe. I am frightened of a low sugar while I am asleep, that is the whole reason, not laziness.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): So the prescribed night dose and what you inject are not the same thing, and we cannot average it. Any proper hypo, sweating, shaking, confusion?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really shaking. Once or twice the head felt empty and I took a sweet, then it passed, but I would not call that a proper low. Mm, I suppose it could have been, sometimes, not really.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will not record those as hypos. About the feet, the counter note from your wife says burning every night since last winter.

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): She spoke because I was still at the scooter. It is not burning, doctor. It is pins and needles, both soles, left more than right, and not every night, only after I have stood all day in the shop, then when I lie down. Since Diwali or after Diwali, I cannot say, and last winter or the one before, that part even she was guessing.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pins and needles in both soles, left worse, after long standing, not nightly burning, and the start you cannot date. Any ulcer, any break in the skin, any black area?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No ulcer, no black patch, I look with a small mirror. The skin gets dry, that is all, especially the heels. I oil them sometimes and sometimes I forget, what to say.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the eyes. Blurring, floaters, trouble with the newspaper?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really. The old spectacles still do for the paper. I would not say the vision has changed, it is the same only.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then I will not write down a vision change. When was the last retina check, the dilated one?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): At a camp by the temple, last winter, or the one before that. They put the drops, I remember the burning of the drops, but the date and what they concluded, the paper is lost. I cannot tell you even the month.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): We will send you for a proper eye check, the date stays open. Any chest pain, or breathlessness when you walk?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Chest pain, no. Breathlessness, um, only if I rush for the bus, and even that—
[SEG0028] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry, doctor, the afternoon lab list is nearly full. Do you want the HbA1c booked today or shall I leave it?
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Book it today, kindly, and I will add the other bloods in a minute. Mr Iyer, you were saying, only when you rush.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, only if I hurry, and it goes when I slow down. Not while I am sitting, not at night. I can manage the shop floor without stopping.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Aside from the diabetes, any blood pressure treatment, heart trouble, kidney trouble?

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): They have said the BP is a little high, but I am on no BP tablet. Kidney, nobody has told me there is a problem. My father had diabetes and he lost one toe, my mother had blood pressure, and for myself no operation, not even the appendix.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Father with diabetes and a toe amputation, mother with hypertension, no surgery for you. Smoking, alcohol, the work?

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Never smoking. Alcohol, a small peg at a wedding only, not a regular habit. I run a stationery shop, on my feet most of the day, and I live with my wife. Meals are rice and dal, and at festival time I do take too many sweets, I am not hiding that.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to a medicine, a rash, swelling?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. They have given penicillin before, no rash, no problem.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Shoes off, please. Both dorsalis pedis pulses are present, there is no ulcer and no broken callus, and the skin is dry with no infection. With the monofilament you miss two points on the left sole and one on the right.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): The left is the one that troubles me more, yes. Also, about the metformin, if I eat late the stomach sometimes—
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Loose motions with it?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Not loose. A little bloating after the night tablet, not every day. I still take it, I have not stopped it ever.

[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mild bloating only, metformin continues. Let me put it together. Longstanding type 2 diabetes, sugars above target, the glargine dose sitting unclear between the label and what you dial, missed on work nights, and sensory change in the feet. My working impression is diabetic neuropathy, provisional, though it could also be pressure from standing all day, and I am not closing that door.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): So you are not sure it is the sugar affecting the nerve.

[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Correct, it stays provisional until the tests speak. Today, HbA1c, creatinine and electrolytes, and a urine albumin, and Kavitha will book all three. I will refer you to the eye clinic for retinal screening. Please do not change the insulin number yourself, bring the pen and the last prescription next time, take the night injection after a proper meal on work days instead of skipping, check and moisturise the feet daily with no barefoot walking in the shop, and write every home sugar with the date.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): I will bring the pen, and the prescription is in the shop drawer under the bill book, or maybe the pooja shelf, I will find it. The Diwali stock I still have to—
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): See me in six weeks with the results. And if the feet become numb all the time or you see a sore, come earlier, don't wait for that visit.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks, yes doctor. Kavitha, the urine bottle, do I do that now or after the blood?
[SEG0047] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Now is fine, I will hand you the bottle, and the bloods are booked for today before you go.

spec.situation: Type 2 diabetic on tablets plus insulin; patient and nurse give different insulin doses, patient skips doses on work days, reads home sugar numbers aloud in a muddled way ('one-eighty-something fasting'). Foot and eye questions.
features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

bad.reason: Uncertain eye-check date is supported, but related entity should be eye screening/history, not referral action.
bad.text: The patient cannot date his last dilated eye check, remembering only a temple camp last winter or the winter before. (type=date_uncertain, related_entities=clinical_actions[3], resolution_status=unresolved)

omissions.text: Insulin glargine/Lantus dose details are incomplete: the pharmacy label says 24 units at bedtime, but the patient says he usually dials 18 units and sometimes 20 if sugar 'felt high'.

Insulin adherence detail: he injects on weekends after dinner but skips the night insulin on work days about 3 to 4 nights per week because he fears nocturnal hypoglycaemia, especially when he has only had biscuits.
Negative finding missing: patient denied any black area/black patch on the feet.
Negative finding missing: patient said he can manage the shop floor without stopping, in the context of exertional breathlessness assessment.
Negative finding missing: no vision change; he said old spectacles still work for reading and vision is 'the same only'.
Possible hypoglycaemia symptoms were discussed: once or twice his 'head felt empty' and he took a sweet and it passed, though the doctor chose not to record these as definite hypos.
Medication tolerance detail missing: metformin causes mild bloating after the night tablet, not every day, and he has never stopped taking it.
Allergy detail incomplete: he specifically reported previous penicillin exposure without rash or problem.
Examination finding missing: the doctor documented no broken callus and no infection on the feet.
Past history detail missing: no operation at all, specifically 'not even the appendix'.
Investigation context missing: the capillary glucose of 214 was explicitly not fasting because he had tea in the waiting area.
